key_insight: Latent PDE mapping transfers PDE residuals and boundary conditions to a common latent geometry, enabling physics-informed models to generalize across unseen shapes with sparse training data.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce the amount of geometry-specific simulation data needed to train surrogate models for complex engineering systems such as cardiac electrophysiology.
method: Map each physical geometry to a predefined latent domain using the deformation gradient.
Pull back PDE residuals and boundary conditions so shape gradients are computed consistently across geometries.
Train physics-informed neural networks and deep operator networks in this latent formulation.
evidence_signal: The authors trained on only 15 geometrically parameterized samples in 2D and 3D and reported about a 4–6× reduction in mean relative L2 error on select geometry families.
watch_item: Benefits were geometry-dependent, with only modest gains for affine and shear-deformed cases, so the approach may not help equally across all deformation types.
paper_title: Latent PDE mapping for efficient physics-informed learning across geometries with limited data
